name: CT witness

structured_output.specificity_hits: 3 system×pathology cells survive BH-FDR<0.05 (over 40 cells, one-sided MWU vs 404 no_pathology controls, Cole/de Lange–corrected age-gap): cardiovascular→vascular d=0.34 (p_FDR=0.003, the pre-expected diagonal); cardiovascular→trauma d=0.30 (p_FDR=0.038); endocrine/reproductive→tumor d=0.19 (p_FDR=0.034). Whole-body clock alone flags vascular (d=0.36, p_FDR=0.003) but cannot localize it; per-system decomposition does. At the single-organ level, 12 organs' corrected age-gaps separate a pathology at FDR<0.05, led by iliac artery→vascular (d up to 0.66); skeletal bridge supported by humerus→trauma d=0.60, vertebra T2→trauma d=0.50, costal cartilages→inflammation d=0.42. bleeding (n=15) correctly non-significant.
structured_output.honest_status: Volume-only clock, rigorously validated: MAE 8.56y (95% CI 8.14–8.97), R²=0.432 (0.38–0.48), 5-fold OOF, HistGradientBoosting on 117 absolute organ volumes, n=1227. Reproduces the green-lit 8.52/0.45 baseline within CI. n=1228 is modest — all metrics are cross-validated with bootstrap CIs; the 89-scan test split is deliberately NOT used. Per-system clocks are individually weak (cardiovascular best R²=0.29, skeletal 0.11, several ≈0) — expected, since one system carries less age signal than the whole body; they exist to localize specificity, not to compete on accuracy. The clock is VOLUME-ONLY: HU/density features (vertebral BMD, muscle/fat attenuation) are the stated upgrade requiring the 22.6GB Images.zip and are documented in ct_methods.md as a separate/parallel track, not run here. Pathology labels are scan-level and coarse; analysis is cross-sectional. All 6 outputs also staged to Google Drive (folder 'Body Across Scales — Witness 2 (CT structural clock)').
